steps.title: Import React, useRef, useImperativeHandle, and forwardRef
steps.instruction: Import React, useRef, useImperativeHandle, and forwardRef from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all four items from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing multiple hooks
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React, useRef, useImperativeHandle, and forwardRef from 'react'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React hooks and utilities are imported for using useImperativeHandle.
successCriteria: React, useRef, useImperativeHandle, and forwardRef are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported all the necessary hooks and utilities for this lesson.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some items, but make sure to include React, useRef, useImperativeHandle, and forwardRef.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're importing React, useRef, useImperativeHandle, and forwardRef from 'react'.

steps.title: Create a child component with forwardRef
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ChildInput that uses forwardRef to accept a ref prop. The component should return an empty <div> element for now.
steps.hint: Use forwardRef to wrap your component function. The component should take props and ref as parameters.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useRef, useImperativeHandle, forwardRef } from 'react';

// Create your ChildInput component with forwardRef here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ChildInput component is created using forwardRef, ready to accept a ref and return a <div>.
successCriteria: ChildInput component is defined using forwardRef and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a forwardRef component. This allows the parent to pass a ref to this child component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using forwardRef and your component returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Remember to use forwardRef and return a <div>.

steps.title: Add input element to child component
steps.instruction: Inside your ChildInput component, return an input element with a placeholder attribute set to 'Type here...'.
steps.hint: The component should return JSX containing a single <input> tag with a placeholder prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildInput component returns an input element with a placeholder.
successCriteria: ChildInput returns a JSX input element with placeholder='Type here...'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the input element to the child component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component returns an <input> with a placeholder attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return an input element with a placeholder.

steps.title: Add useImperativeHandle to child component
steps.instruction: Inside your ChildInput component, add the useImperativeHandle hook to expose a focus method on the ref.
steps.hint: Call useImperativeHandle inside the component body, passing the ref and a function that returns an object with a focus method.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildInput component will have a useImperativeHandle hook that defines a focus method to expose via the ref.
successCriteria: useImperativeHandle is called inside ChildInput with the ref parameter and returns an object containing a focus method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added useImperativeHandle to expose a focus method from the child component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure useImperativeHandle is called with the ref and returns an object with a focus method.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added useImperativeHandle inside ChildInput with the correct parameters and return value.

steps.title: Define exposed methods in useImperativeHandle
steps.instruction: Inside the useImperativeHandle hook in your ChildInput component, return an object with a method named 'focus' that calls the focus() method on the input element's DOM node.
steps.hint: The useImperativeHandle hook should return an object. The 'focus' method inside that object should call inputRef.current.focus().
steps.expectedOutcome: The useImperativeHandle hook now exposes a 'focus' method that the parent component can call through the ref.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the exposed method that the parent can call to focus the input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure useImperativeHandle returns an object with a 'focus' method that calls inputRef.current.focus().
steps.feedbackWrong: The useImperativeHandle hook should return an object with a 'focus' method that calls focus() on the input element.

steps.title: Create parent App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that will serve as the parent component. Make it return an empty div for now.
steps.hint:
Define a component called App using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax, and have it return a
element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty div element.
successCriteria: App component is defined as a function
App component returns a div element
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the parent App component. This will serve as the container for our child component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined the App component and it returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined yet. Create a function called App that returns a div element.

steps.title: Initialize ref in parent component
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a ref called childRef using the useRef hook.
steps.hint: Call useRef() and assign it to a variable named childRef.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a ref in a component
const myRef = useRef();
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a ref variable ready to reference the child component.
successCriteria: The App component contains a childRef variable initialized with useRef().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ref in the parent component. This ref will allow you to access the child's exposed methods.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the useRef hook inside the App component and naming the variable childRef.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the useRef hook correctly inside the App component and naming the variable childRef.

steps.title: Add child component to parent with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your App component, render the ChildInput component and pass the childRef as the ref prop.
steps.hint: Add <ChildInput ref={childRef} /> inside the div after the heading.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: rendering a component with a ref
<MyComponent ref={myRef} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component now renders the child component and passes the ref to it, establishing the connection for imperative handle usage.
successCriteria: ChildInput is rendered inside the App component's return statement with the ref prop set to childRef.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the ChildInput component and passed the ref to it. This connects the parent's ref to the child component, allowing the parent to access the child's exposed methods.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're rendering ChildInput with the ref prop correctly. Check that you're using the exact component name and passing childRef as the ref attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child component isn't rendered with the ref prop correctly. Remember to add <ChildInput ref={childRef} /> inside the div in the App component's return statement.

steps.title: Add button to trigger child focus
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Focus Child Input' and wire its onClick handler to call childRef.current.focus().
steps.hint: Place the button after the ChildInput component. Use the onClick attribute and call childRef.current.focus() inside an arrow function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button that triggers a function
<button onClick={() => someRef.current.doSomething()}>
  Trigger Action
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Focus Child Input' appears below the input field. When clicked, it focuses the child input field using the exposed focus method.
successCriteria: Button element with text 'Focus Child Input' is present
Button is placed inside the App component's return statement
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added a button that triggers the child component's focus method through the ref. This demonstrates how useImperativeHandle allows parent components to call specific methods on child components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your button has the correct text and the onClick handler properly calls childRef.current.focus(). Remember to use an arrow function for the onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't working as expected. Check that you've added a button element with the text 'Focus Child Input' and that its onClick handler calls childRef.current.focus().

steps.title: Export the App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export so it can be rendered.
steps.hint: Use the default export syntax at the end of your file.
steps.analogousExample:
// Exporting a component as default
export default App;
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported and ready to be used as the main component.
successCriteria: App component is exported as default.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've exported the App component, making it available for rendering.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the default export syntax for the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component needs to be exported as default. Check the export syntax.
